content.title: Management of acute decompensated heart failure and acute pulmonary oedema
content.figure_summary: Figure 7: Flowchart for management of acute decompensated heart failure. Starts with congestion/fluid overload leading to assessment for hypoperfusion. For predominant congestion: loop diuretics (Class I) with escalation (increase dose and/or combine diuretics, Class IIa) if needed; if diuretic resistance or end-stage renal failure consider renal replacement therapy (Class IIa) or palliative care. For hypoperfusion with congestion: loop diuretics (Class I) plus consider inotropes (Class IIb); if persistent hypoperfusion or organ damage consider vasopressors (eg, norepinephrine) (Class IIb). For refractory cases consider mechanical circulatory support (MCS, Class IIa) and/or renal replacement therapy (Class IIa) or palliative care.
management_flow: Assess patient with acute decompensated heart failure for congestion/fluid overload and hypoperfusion.
If congestion predominant: start loop diuretics (Class I).
If inadequate response: increase diuretic doses and/or combine diuretics (Class IIa).
If diuretic resistance or end-stage renal failure: consider renal replacement therapy (Class IIa) or palliative care.
If hypoperfusion present alongside congestion: give loop diuretics (Class I) and consider inotropes (Class IIb).
If persistent hypoperfusion/organ damage: consider vasopressors (eg, norepinephrine) (Class IIb).
For refractory cardiogenic shock consider MCS (Class IIa) and/or renal replacement therapy (Class IIa) or palliative care.

first_line_therapies: Oxygen: continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP), non-invasive positive-pressure ventilation and/or high-flow nasal cannula
Intravenous vasodilators if systolic blood pressure (SBP) is high to reduce left ventricular afterload
advanced_cases: In advanced heart failure with low cardiac output, consider inotropes, vasopressors, and/or mechanical circulatory support to restore organ perfusion

additional_recommendations: Adequate diuretic doses to relieve congestion and close monitoring of diuresis is recommended regardless of perfusion status.
Identify and treat precipitating causes and decongest as priority; correct hypoperfusion when present.
content.references_and_notes: Figure and text reference guideline classifications (Class I, IIa, IIb) and examples (eg, norepinephrine as vasopressor).
